ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
As shown in the figure, object A with mass $m_{1}=1\mathrm{kg}$ is suspended by three light strings $O A$, $O B$, and $O C$, with the junction point at $O$. The angle between string $O A$ and the vertical direction is $\theta=60^{\circ}$. String $O B$ is horizontal and its end $B$ is connected to object B with mass $m_{2}=4\mathrm{kg}$ placed on a horizontal table. String $O C$ is vertical and its end $C$ is connected to object A. Both objects A and B are at rest. Take $g=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$.

1. Find the magnitude of the tension force produced by the light rope $O A$.
2. Find the magnitude and direction of the frictional force acting on object B.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, a block labeled Object B sits on a horizontal table on the left. A horizontal string runs from the right side of Object B to the junction point O. From O, a vertical string goes downward to a hanging block labeled Object A. Another string from O goes obliquely upward to the right to a fixed support, and the angle between this inclined string and a vertical dashed reference line is marked as θ. Thus O is a three-string junction: OB is horizontal, OC is vertical, and OA is inclined at θ = 60° to the vertical. Reasoning: Draw free-body diagrams. For the hanging object A, it is at rest, so the vertical rope OC must support its weight: T_OC = m1 g = 1 × 10 = 10 N. At the massless junction O, the three tensions balance. The inclined rope tension T_OA has vertical component T_OA cos 60° and horizontal component T_OA sin 60°. Vertical equilibrium of O gives T_OA cos 60° = T_OC = 10 N, so T_OA = 10 / cos 60° = 20 N. Horizontal equilibrium of O gives T_OB = T_OA sin 60° = 20 × (√3/2) = 10√3 N. For object B on the table, the rope OB pulls it horizontally toward O, i.e. to the right in the figure. Since object B is at rest, static friction must balance this pull, so its magnitude is T_OB = 10√3 N and its direction is to the left.
